en: Thus is the procedure for the painted maṇḍala. Since this procedure of painting bears fruit only when the rite is performed mentally, the mental procedure alone is superior. Therefore, one should perform everything mentally—beginning with the appropriation of the site and assuming the form of the Lord of the Maṇḍala, and ending with the consecration of the images and so forth, the initiation of the disciples, the dismissal, and the rites of pacification and fire-offerings (homa).

Therefore, when all this cannot be performed, is not appropriate, or is not obtained due to some deficiency, then everything should be performed through meditation alone. For even when external objects are present, meditation itself is primary; external ritual is desired only for the sake of increasing merit through the world’s seeing, giving, and faith. However, due to a lack of necessary materials, every rite must be performed by meditating alone. As it has been said by the ancient masters: [NB VĀ adds].

Thus, this is the ritual for the drawn mandala; however, the ritual performed through mental engagement alone is endowed with the fruit—therefore, the mental ritual itself is supreme. Consequently, [it includes] the appropriation of the site and so forth by means of the form of the Lord of the Mandala, as well as the consecration of images and the like.

One should mentally perform everything up to the initiation of the disciple, the request for departure, and the conclusion of the peaceful fire offering (*śānti-homa*). For this very reason, whenever it is impossible to perform these because one lacks certain requisites, or when it is improper or unavailable, one should perform them all through mental visualization.

Even regarding the existence of external objects, meditative concentration alone is primary. Because it is seen by the world, people desire external rituals solely for the purpose of increasing merit through faith in generosity and so forth. However, one who is devoid of material requisites should accomplish all rituals through intention alone.
Thus it has been said: "When all things are non-existent, one should conceptualize them only through meditation. As it is stated:
"If all entities have become non-existent, one should thoroughly investigate by means of thought alone."

Therefore, even a beginner with a steady mind should perform the consecration and other rites within a mentally emanated maṇḍala, and should confer initiation upon a worthy person. Thus it is said in the *Buddhakapāla-tantra*:
"Within the center of the lotus of wisdom is a maṇḍala of ten million yojanas;
in that three-layered maṇḍala, the wise one should sprinkle the excellent disciple. It is also stated elsewhere:
"In some cases, the performance of the true maṇḍala ritual is intended by the Victors to be done with the mind alone. Thus it is said.

Therefore, even a beginner, with a stable mind, should perform the consecration and other rites within the mentally emanated maṇḍala, and should also confer the manifest empowerment upon fortunate beings. Thus, it is said in the glorious Buddhakapāla Tantra: "Within the lotus of wisdom, in a maṇḍala of ten million yojanas..."

It is said: "In the center of that maṇḍala of the three families, the wise one should confer initiation upon the disciple. Furthermore, it is stated elsewhere: "The Victor intended for the maṇḍala to be performed in some cases by means of the mind alone.
Thus is the mental procedure for the maṇḍala (*mānaso maṇḍalavidhiḥ*).
This is the ritual for the mental maṇḍala.
